props.title: The query languages — and the standard that's unifying them

left.head: Cypher & GQL
rows: GQL: the 2024 ISO standard — SQL for graphs.
The default for operational graph apps.

right.head: SPARQL
rows: The W3C standard for querying triples.
Federates across many endpoints at once.
Pairs with OWL inference and SHACL.
The default when meaning must be portable.

props.foot: GQL is doing for graphs what SQL did for tables — one standard everyone can target.

props.title: Who can see and do what — enforced on the graph

cards.head: Relationship-level access
cards.body: Hide sensitive nodes and edges per role — the ontology's security dimension, made real.

cards.head: PII & compliance
cards.body: Tag sensitive nodes; lineage proves exactly where regulated data flows, for audits.

cards.head: Change control
cards.body: Version the ontology and review changes to meaning like you review changes to code.

props.foot: Once agents act on the graph, governance is the line between a system that helps and one that harms.

props.title: Monitor the graph like a production service

cards.head: Quality metrics
cards.body: Track orphan nodes, duplicate rate, and constraint violations over time — a dashboard for the graph itself.

cards.head: Drift alerts
cards.body: If extraction quality drops, page someone. The graph is a product with an SLA, not a side project.

cards.head: Golden queries
cards.body: A suite of known-answer queries runs on every build — integration tests, but for meaning.

props.foot: You already monitor your services. Monitor the graph the same way — everything now leans on it.
Uber ETAs, Pinterest recs, fraud rings, drug discovery — all learned on graph structure.
